sources.note: Nothing on stress; Tagin only named among tribes. p.457: 'Phonemic tone is not a prevalent feature. While completely non-existent in such eastern languages as Bokar, lexically significant pitch occurs to varying degrees in many Western languages' (Bengni, Gallong, Apatani examples; nothing Tagin-specific).

sources.citation: Namkung, Ju (ed.). 1996. Phonological Inventories of Tibeto-Burman Languages. STEDT Monograph 3. Berkeley: STEDT. Tagin entry p.358 (digest of Das Gupta 1983, data from Taliha, Sippy valley).

sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.358: 'Vowel length is apparently significant, but is not marked.' / 'Tagin seems to be a tone language ([KDG-Tag] lists minimal pairs), but tone is not marked.' (second-hand from Das Gupta 1983).
